set: Rift Parade — Wrong Side of Reality
note: Identity fields (id, name, rarity, type, episode, art) are from the production pack and must not change. Gameplay fields are Claude Code's and may be tuned. Alternate printings share the base card's gameplay.

cards.name: Kai, Errand Runner
cards.art: Kai racing through rainy Kurohama alleys with an undelivered parcel; first canonical male lead shot.

text: Momentum (+1 Power for each Technique you played this turn, up to +3)
Next Episode: may be played on a Character you control named Kai that costs less, paying the difference.
gameplay.purpose: Cheap Kinetic body: gets bigger every Technique you play, so it is a real threat in Technique-heavy decks and a poor one elsewhere.

cards.name: Late-Shift Dispatcher
cards.art: Sleepy adult courier dispatcher slides an anonymous job ticket through a service window.

text: When this enters: Look at the top 2 cards of your deck; put any on the bottom.
gameplay.purpose: Smoothing for any deck: a sturdy blocker that fixes the next two draws.

cards.name: Paper-Mouthed Imp
cards.art: Little toothy Rift creature chewing street maps, never a cute normal animal.

text: This Character has Phase while the Rift is 3 or more.
gameplay.purpose: Fragile one-drop that becomes hard to block once the Rift is wide; rewards decks that raise the Rift and loses its edge when it is mended.

cards.name: Kurohama Backstreets
cards.art: Rain-slick vending machines and elevated tracks above cramped pedestrian lanes.

text: Characters with cost 2 or less you control get +1/0.
gameplay.purpose: Aggro zone: all your cheap Characters hit harder. Replaced or Severed when the opponent has a better reality.

cards.name: Address That Isn't There
cards.art: Delivery slip bearing an impossible changing street number; clear legible prop.

text: Act (1 energy, once per turn): Step target Character you control.
gameplay.purpose: Positioning engine: a second free Step each turn, to dodge removal, set up blockers or bring a Backstage ability onto the Stage.

cards.name: Momentum Skip
cards.art: Kai redirects his own falling weight to leap across an alley.

text: Target Character you control moves Backstage and all damage to it is prevented this turn. (Reaction)
gameplay.purpose: Cheap protection: pulls one Character Backstage and prevents damage to it this turn (a Kinetic leap).

cards.name: Nova, Passing Stranger
cards.art: Silver-haired Nova half emerging from a magenta seam in an overpass shadow.

text: When this enters: Return 1 card(s) from your Rift pool to your hand.
Next Episode: may be played on a Character you control named Nova that costs less, paying the difference.
gameplay.purpose: Navigation tempo: returns one slipped card to hand, so a late Nova lets you re-use a key card instead of keeping it as energy.

cards.name: Hard Stop
cards.art: Kai catches a flying road sign mid-impact with a red shock ring.

text: Prevent all combat damage dealt by one attacking enemy Character, then deal 2 damage to it. (Reaction)
gameplay.purpose: Defensive Kinetic answer: stops one attacker's damage and punishes it. Keeps Technique decks alive against big attackers.

cards.name: Fracture Compass
cards.art: Battered pocket compass needle points upward toward a ceiling crack.

text: Act (1 energy, once per turn): Look at the top 1 card of your deck; put any on the bottom, then raise or lower the Rift by 1.
gameplay.purpose: Rift dial: lets a deck steer the shared Rift gauge up or down by one each turn while smoothing its draws.

cards.name: Overpass at Dawn
cards.art: Empty freeway spans and thin pink fracture across cloud cover.

text: Characters with Phase you control get +1/0.
At your wake: Raise the Rift by 1.
gameplay.purpose: Rift deck zone: widens the Rift every turn and rewards Phase Characters; speeds up Anomalies for everyone, so it is a commitment.

cards.name: Mika, Salvage Runner
cards.art: Blond ponytailed adult mechanic Mika carrying a tool case through scrapyard gates.

text: When this enters: Search your deck for a Relic with cost 2 or less and put it into your hand.
Next Episode: may be played on a Character you control named Mika that costs less, paying the difference.
gameplay.purpose: Workshop engine starter: finds the Relic the deck wants.

cards.name: Copperback Gremlin
cards.art: Broad-mouthed machinery pest made of wire, bolts and stolen brake pads.

text: When this is defeated: Deal 1 damage to target enemy Character.
gameplay.purpose: Aggressive trader: dies for value, so blocking it or trading with it always costs something.

cards.name: Temporary Spark
cards.art: Mika imbues a wrench with supernatural charge mid-repair.

text: Target Character you control gets +2/+0 until end of turn, then if you control 1 or more Relic: It gets +0/+1 until end of turn. (Reaction)
gameplay.purpose: Combat trick: Imbue a Character. Better if you control a Relic. Also feeds Momentum.

cards.name: Secondhand Sky Yard
cards.art: Stacked tram cars, salvage cranes and a makeshift workshop.

text: Your Relics cost 1 less.
Your imbued Relics get +1/+1.
gameplay.purpose: Workshop zone: cheaper Relics, stronger animated Relics.

cards.name: Ayame, Ghost Hunter
cards.art: Black-haired adult swordswoman Ayame watching spectral tracks from a rooftop.

text: Sever (can block Phase; Characters it damages are silenced)
Next Episode: may be played on a Character you control named Ayame that costs less, paying the difference.
gameplay.purpose: Cheap answer to Phase and abilities: the only common that blocks Phase attackers.

cards.name: Thread-Eater Specter

text: Phase (can be blocked only by Phase or Sever Characters; no effect at Rift 0-2 or while Marked)

cards.name: Clean Sever
cards.art: Single exact sword cut separates a ghostly tether from a lamp post.

text: Sever: destroy a Condition or the Zone, then draw a card.
gameplay.purpose: Clean answer to a Condition or the Zone, and it replaces itself.

cards.name: Abandoned Shrine Steps

cards.name: Mistaken Accomplice

text: Attach to an enemy Stage Character. The host's controller may pay 2 energy to remove it.
